title: Extraction and Drop
premise: Coral Oyelaran, a financial-crimes investigator who testified against the Voss laundering network and has lived under witness protection for three years, discovers his safe house listed online — interior photos, his own books on the shelf, a viewing scheduled for Saturday. The listing is a message: someone inside protection sold him out, and the 'accidental gas explosion' planned for the open house will erase him and the evidence he still holds. Racing to trace who leaked the address through a chain of shell companies, Coral is forced to trust a disgraced former colleague, Nkechi Adeyemi, and a teenage hacker, Milo, who becomes the found family he never let himself want. The climax comes at the open house itself, where Coral turns the trap around, exposing the mole — his own handler — and forcing the network's accountant to surrender the ledger that names everyone. In the end, Coral chooses testimony over invisibility, trading the safety of erasure for a life that is finally, deliberately visible.
about_author: Felix Villalobos is a former compliance analyst who spent a decade tracing money through shells and safe houses before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers about people whose careful lives come apart in a single afternoon.

chapters.title: The House That Wasn't Empty
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Insomniac Coral scrolls listings at 3 a.m. and finds his safe house photographed from inside — his mug on the counter, his mother's scarf on the chair. Emotional beat: cold dread; the illusion of safety shatters in a single image.

chapters.title: Clean Money
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, flashback-tinged. We learn his casework against the Voss network, the incident that killed his partner Dara, and why he can't sleep. He reports the listing to his handler, Marsh, who dismisses it as a glitch. Beat: guilt wearing the mask of routine.

chapters.title: Viewing Saturday
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The listing shows an open house this weekend. Marsh promises relocation but stalls. Coral notices the listing agent's license belongs to a man dead since 2019. Beat: paranoia sharpening into method — the investigator wakes up.

chapters.title: Nkechi
chapters.summary: Nkechi's POV. A disgraced ex-colleague now doing forensic accounting for insurers spots the same listing while pricing a claim on the property. She recognizes the address from the Voss trial files and drives toward Coral instead of away. Beat: reluctant loyalty rekindled.

chapters.title: The Mole's Fingerprints
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Coral and Nkechi meet at a diner; she confirms the listing traces through three shells to a holding company with Voss-family fingerprints. Someone with access to protection files fed them the address. Beat: two lonely people choosing each other.

chapters.title: Milo Breaks In
chapters.summary: Milo's POV. A seventeen-year-old hacker squatting in the safe house's garage apartment — placed there as an unofficial extra set of eyes by a paranoid predecessor — reveals he's been logging visitors for months. Beat: comic relief curdling into stakes; the kid knows too much.

chapters.title: Gas Line
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A utility crew inspects the house unannounced; Coral photographs their truck and runs the plates — a company registered eleven days ago. The attack won't be a shooting; it will be an accident with paperwork. Beat: the horror of bureaucratic murder.

chapters.title: What Dara Left Me
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, memory-heavy. Going through Dara's effects, Coral finds a burner phone she hid before dying — unsent drafts naming someone inside the marshals' chain. Beat: grief transformed into inheritance; he owes her the truth.

chapters.title: Marsh Calls Twice
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Marsh urges Coral to accept immediate transfer to a new identity — no trial, no testimony, just disappear. The offer is too convenient. Coral realizes the relocation could be the kill box. Beat: betrayal glimpsed but not yet proven.

chapters.title: Shell Game
chapters.summary: Nkechi's POV. She peels the corporate onion in a hotel room war-map of printouts: the dead agent, the gas company, and a payments trail all touch one law firm — which also employs Marsh's brother-in-law. Beat: the net tightening; hope with teeth.

chapters.title: Run, Kid
chapters.summary: Milo's POV. Men sweep the neighborhood photographing houses. Milo wipes his servers and bolts with one drive, leading them away from Coral. Beat: the found family paying forward; terror and courage in a teenager's sneakers.

chapters.title: The Ledger Keeper
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Following Dara's drafts, Coral finds Anselm Voss-Ruiz, the network's frightened accountant, hiding in plain sight as a marina bookkeeper. Anselm admits the Saturday 'gas leak' was signed off weeks ago. Beat: the clock becomes audible.

chapters.title: Safe House No More
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Coral abandons protection entirely, going dark with Nkechi and a returned, bruised Milo. Marsh declares Coral unstable and puts out an alert. Beat: burning the last bridge; freedom and exposure at once.

chapters.title: Interrogation of One
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Alone in a motel, Coral replays every conversation with Marsh and finds the tell — Marsh always knew details never reported. He records a confession-to-camera naming his suspicion. Beat: the investigator investigating himself; clarity like a blade.

chapters.title: Anselm's Price
chapters.summary: Nkechi's POV. Anselm will surrender the full ledger only if his daughter is extracted first. Nkechi runs the extraction herself, a tense night op through marina cameras. Beat: competence as love; the team becomes real.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The ledger names forty accounts, four banks, and — devastatingly — the protection-program liaison who sold addresses: not Marsh, but Marsh's boss, Deputy Director Hale. Beat: the ground shifts again; the enemy wears the flag.

chapters.title: Saturday Morning
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Open-house day. Balloons, coffee urns, a gas crew working the line. Coral walks in as a buyer, wired, while Nkechi feeds timing to a journalist and Milo jams the crew's remote detonator signal. Beat: held breath.

chapters.title: Extraction and Drop
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, climax. Hale arrives to watch his clean accident. Coral baits him into confessing on tape, the detonation fails, and Hale orders his crew openly — recorded by thirty phones and one federal witness. Beat: the trap inverted; visibility as weapon.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Loud
chapters.summary: Nkechi's POV. Arrests ripple outward; Marsh, complicit through silence, cooperates. Coral's recording goes to prosecutors, and his protected status dissolves into something stranger: a public witness with a name. Beat: exhaustion after adrenaline; the cost counted.

chapters.title: What the House Sold
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral visits the empty house one last time, buys nothing, leaves the scarf behind for Dara. He sleeps — actually sleeps — for the first time in three years. Beat: mourning completed; memory laid down like a tool.

chapters.title: Found
chapters.summary: Milo's POV. Milo gets a legal guardianship petition — filed by Coral — and rants about it while clearly thrilled. Nkechi takes a job rebuilding the corrupted case files. Beat: warmth without sentimentality; family chosen in paperwork.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, final chapter. On the courthouse steps before testifying, cameras find him and he doesn't flinch. He thinks of Dara, of the mug in the photo, of the house that gave him back his name. Beat: inheritance accepted; a life lived in the open.
